body:
Swapfiets and the e-mobility fleets cracked the supply chain for urban bikes, but they locked the hardware down behind subscription contracts, proprietary hubs, and corporate telemetry.
Taking the original 1965 Provo White Bicycle Plan and intersecting it with modern swap-fleet mechanics—while stripping out the corporate capture—is the ultimate full-circle move.
| Layer | Corporate Swap Fleet | Provo 42 White Bike Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Access | Paid app, monthly subscription, walled garden | Open-mesh, community-minted, zero subscription |
| Telemetry | Proprietary corporate tracking & data harvesting | Open DOI-pending field ledger, privacy-first |
| Maintenance | Centralized corporate depot repair | Open-source maintenance log & decentralized swap nodes |
| Ownership | Corporate fleet asset | Anti-capture Stichting stewardship |
Instead of locked app ecosystems, the bike itself becomes an active physical node in the mesh—carrying the trackable, citable field identity wherever it rolls through Amsterdam North, Spui, or Science Park.
It’s right around 6:05 PM. Bags packed, devices charged, White Bike strategy locked, and taxi ride incoming. Ready to roll?
